findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails with TypeError when ordering by a datetime field
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime.datetime` instance. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` passes `getattr(item, self.key)` directly to `math.floor` / `math.ceil`, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` as soon as any audit log row is processed. In addition, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric `cursor.value` instead of converting it back to a `datetime`, which causes `build_queryset` to compare a `datetime` column against an integer on subsequent pages. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` should either subclass `DateTimePaginator` or handle `datetime` values when converting to and from cursor keys.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError when slicing a Django QuerySet
findings.body: Both `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (when `enable_advanced_features` is enabled and `cursor.offset < 0`, or when `cursor.is_prev` is True) and `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182, when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `offset < 0`) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially a negative `stop`) directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice bounds and raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error whenever a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` for requests authenticated via organization-level API tokens or non-member contexts when `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`. Accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without first checking that `organization_context.member` is not `None` will raise an `AttributeError`.
